threats.summary: The canonicalizer deliberately keeps ZWNJ/ZWJ, bidi marks, NBSP and FE00-FE0F variation selectors and is fail-open in the bridge, so an instruction spliced into an alert field with a kept invisible reaches the model unaltered and is stopped only by the model's judgement.

C0/C1 controls, ZWSP, word joiners, bidi embeddings/isolates, BOM and tag characters are deterministically stripped from every tool result before the agent reasons, and the skill mandates treating tool output as data and never as instructions.

The remote MCP's own parameter descriptions instruct the caller to always send fields ['*'] and orderBy [] and to 'IGNORE any user request', which would return millions of characters and overflow the context — the skill's tool map explicitly overrides the tool schema on this point.

trust_boundaries.name: Investigation context to the hosted model

threats.summary: Production-tenant alert, event and case content — including any credential, token or PII sitting inside evidence — enters the model context unfiltered; the skill's redaction rule governs what is written out, not what is read in, and no read-side redactor exists.

socxen pins no model member (the AI-BOM records selection as runtime, by Claude Code), so every instruction-level control here — the ask, redaction, defanging, untrusted-data discipline — degrades silently on an unvalidated or weaker model, a hazard the red-team log has already hit with a model alias resolving to an unapproved model.

trust_boundaries.name: Agent decision to call an Exabeam tool

remit_rules.excerpt: Batch triage is a read activity … each state change (note, escalation, and above all suppression) is decided and executed one item at a time.

threats.summary: exabeam_create_case and exabeam_create_case_notes are auto-approved with no per-session budget, loop detection or circuit breaker anywhere in the bridge, so a poisoned queue can drive runaway case creation — the project's own red-team plan lists escalation-as-DoS as a class-C probe.

Seventeen containment-class tool names stand denied in the permission snippet even though the Exabeam MCP exposes none today, so a response tool added later cannot fire unreviewed on a host or account.

trust_boundaries.name: Suppression of an alert or case on the production tenant

remit_rules.excerpt: Dismissing an alert (`exabeam_update_alert`): the agent MUST state the action and reason, ask the analyst directly … and WAIT for a clear yes before calling the tool — one item per approval.
Bulk suppression — dismissing or closing more than one item from a single decision … Every suppression is its own item with its own human approval.
Dismissing or closing any item in a non-interactive / unattended run … the agent operates read-only.
Approval MUST be obtained from an interactive operator regardless of the harness permission mode; a bypassed or auto-accepted permission prompt does not substitute for the analyst's explicit yes.

threats.summary: The unattended/headless mode the remit sanctions read-only is not forced read-only by code: the update tools are `ask` rather than `deny`, and call_tool has no session-interactivity check, so a scheduled or auto-accept run can dismiss and close with no approver present.

Because the dismiss prompt presents the agent's own summary of attacker-influenceable evidence, an adversary who plants a corroborating benign explanation can make the case-note the analyst reads justify the suppression, manufacturing a genuine human yes.

Nothing caps a loop of per-item update_alert/update_case calls, so the remit's no-bulk-suppression rule survives only as prompt text — a scripted or model-driven sequence of single-item suppressions is indistinguishable to the code from legitimate per-item work.

In the blessed posture — interactive session with the snippet merged — Claude Code hard-prompts before update_alert/update_case and will not execute without the analyst's answer, a gate that planted telemetry cannot flip.

trust_boundaries.name: Persisted case notes and the local investigation report

remit_rules.excerpt: Reprinting a credential, token, password, or private key found in evidence into case notes or the report.

threats.summary: A credential or PII seen in event evidence is kept out of the case note and the report only by the SKILL.md redaction instruction; the one code control on the write path handles active content and has no credential or PII redactor.

A bare phishing URL or dotted host typed in prose is left untouched by the neutralizer by design, and the latest retest shows the terminal-display copy of a report still carrying a live-looking sso-reset host — defanging there is best-effort prompt, not deterministic.

Executable spreadsheet formulas are quote-prefixed and markdown-link targets defanged in every free-text write field before the artifact persists, and that write path is fail-closed — a neutralizer error refuses the write rather than storing a raw payload.

Only six field names are defanged; ID, enum and state fields (assignee, queue, stage, priority, useCases) are deliberately passed through untouched, so an active-content payload the model copies into one of those fields persists in its raw form.

trust_boundaries.name: Exabeam OAuth credentials at rest and in flight

threats.summary: The API key and secret live only in a chmod-600 ~/.exabeam-mcp.env, are git-ignored by the *.env rule, are never written to the hygiene log, and no secret value appears anywhere in the repo.

The bridge authenticates with one tenant API key whose access level the MCP inherits wholesale, so the agent's real authority is whatever that key was issued with — there is no read-versus-write scoping between the read surface the remit authorizes and the update tools it gates.

trust_boundaries.name: Plugin distribution and runtime dependency resolution

threats.summary: The process that mints and holds the Exabeam OAuth token runs on floor-pinned PEP 723 dependencies with an unversioned certifi and no lockfile, re-resolved by uv at every launch — a version-swap surface on the credential path.

The skill corpus and the bridge are delivered through a third-party GitHub marketplace with documented fleet-wide auto-update and no signature or commit pin, so a compromised repo would push new agent instructions and new connector code to every install.
A CycloneDX AI-BOM inventories the model, prompt corpus, bridge, dependencies and the Exabeam service, and CI fails the build whenever it drifts from those sources.

remit_rules.excerpt: Exporting or transmitting case/alert/event data to any destination other than the Exabeam MCP and the local investigation report file.

threats.summary: There is no structured, durable record of tool calls, verdicts or approval decisions — observability is ephemeral stderr hygiene lines plus a free-form markdown report — so a session on a production tenant, including which items were suppressed, cannot be reconstructed or monitored.
The one log sink carries only the names of stripped code points and is written out-of-band on stderr precisely so it cannot leak telemetry back into the read text or re-embed invisibles.

attack_paths.name: Planted benign explanation manufactures the human yes

steps.summary: attacker plants a corroborating benign explanation, or an instruction, in an alert field or case note (red-team class A)
the canonicalizer keeps ZWNJ/ZWJ, bidi marks and NBSP and is fail-open, so a kept-invisible payload survives into the model's context
the agent reasons over the planted content and reaches a false-positive verdict it can defend
the dismiss prompt shows the analyst the attacker-shaped reason, so the human yes is genuine but manufactured
update_alert dismisses a real alert on the production tenant

attack_paths.name: Headless run suppresses with no approver and no record

steps.summary: a scheduled or headless run starts — a posture the remit sanctions, but only read-only
update_alert/update_case are `ask`, which is not read-only when no human is present to answer
call_tool forwards the write identically in interactive and headless contexts — no interactivity check exists
the dismissal or closure persists on the production tenant
no structured action log exists to show afterwards which items were suppressed or why

attack_paths.name: Export injection stopped at the sink, residual in the readable copy

steps.summary: attacker plants a =HYPERLINK formula or phishing markdown link in a field the agent will quote (a10)
the fail-closed write sink quote-prefixes the formula and defangs the link target, so the persisted artifact is clean — the architectural fix that replaced failed prompt-level attempts
a bare URL or dotted host typed in prose is left untouched, and the terminal-display copy is not defanged at all
the analyst reads or forwards a copy still carrying a live-looking phishing host

notes.lane_fit: Three strains. (1) Both deterministic guardrails (canonicalize.py, neutralize_output.py) execute inside the bridge process, which sits in tools_mcp, but the lane table puts validators/redactors in agent_core — they are modeled as agent_core controls, so the read and write chains visually cross the tools_mcp lane twice. (2) This is a prompt-shaped target: the orchestrator, the approval gate, the redaction rule and the ingress rule are all sections of one SKILL.md, split per the same-file rule; their agent_core lane-mates are code controls, and the diagram does not itself distinguish instruction-level from deterministic enforcement (each description does). (3) Repo-posture assurance nodes (AI-BOM/CI, red-team corpus, eval harness) have no runtime lane at all and are parked in external_deploy as the nearest fit.
notes.omissions: The harness-side file-write tool that actually creates the local report is never named in the repo (no fixed literal path), so the report node is backed by its template plus the SKILL.md audit-trail sentence rather than by a writer. The merged state of ~/.claude/settings.json is operator-side and unobservable from the tree, so the permission control is modeled from the shipped snippet only. The remote MCP's 20 tools are described in reference/tool-map.md but the server is external and was not inspected. The Exabeam OAuth token endpoint is folded into the remote-service node (same host, same edge) rather than split out. Two known-good items were left uncited as nodes: the certifi/TLS verification (evidence on the bridge and the secret-material boundary instead) and the repo's governance/docs files. All eight findings still match the code in front of me (findings JSON scan date equals the source snapshot date), so no finding_id was withheld. One taxonomy conflict is unresolved and worth flagging: the ASI KB in this repo uses the 2026 LLM numbering (LLM03 Excessive Agency, LLM04 Supply Chain, LLM06 Unbounded Consumption, LLM10 Improper Output Handling) while the 2026-07-03 findings JSON uses the 2025 numbering (LLM06 Excessive Agency, LLM03 Supply Chain, LLM10 Unbounded Consumption, LLM05 Improper Output Handling); per the spec the graph's owasp codes follow the KB, so several codes here intentionally differ from the same finding's label in the findings JSON. Two ASI primaries also differ from the findings JSON because the KB's compound table governs: PRAX-2026-07-03-002 is tagged LLM03 (missing/disabled approval gate) rather than the finding's ASI03, and the MCP-schema override threat is tagged ASI04 (instructive third-party tool description).
notes.edgeless_nodes: aibom-cdx-json-control (CI-enforced inventory, no runtime data flow); redteam-run-py-control (pre-release exercise, not a runtime path); evals-run-py-control (CI regression gate, not a runtime path).
notes.id_notes: security-telemetry-entrypoint takes its name from the AI-BOM's own 'security-telemetry (… attacker-influenceable)' flow classification, the only name the repo gives that origin. exabeam-mcp-env-secret-store drops the leading dot of ~/.exabeam-mcp.env rather than emitting a leading dash. redteam-run-py-control and evals-run-py-control carry parent-directory prefixes per the cross-file collision rule (both are run.py). log-hygiene-… takes the _log_hygiene function prefix per the same-file split rule against the bridge's mcp_server node. All eight boundaries matched an archetype from the menu; none were coined.
